parole.significato: The central seed or "germinating matrix" of a culture.
parole.testo: From Swahili asili (“origin”); introduced in this sense by Marimba Ani.

parole.significato: A member of a local African military or police unit, usually one serving in a European colonial force.
parole.testo: From Swahili askari (“soldier”), from Arabic عَسْكَرِيّ (ʕaskariyy). Doublet of lascar.
Borrowed from Swahili bwana (“master”), from Arabic أَبُونَا (ʔabūnā, “our father”). Doublet of abbot.

parole.significato: Blood (a member of the Los Angeles gang the Bloods)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili damu (“blood”), borrowed from Arabic دَم (dam, “blood”), from Proto-Semitic *dam-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *dam-.

parole.significato: A medicine, particularly a native one or one used by witch doctors.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili dawa (“medicine”), borrowed from Arabic دَوَاء (dawāʔ).

parole.significato: A woolen robe worn by Arabs.
parole.testo: Derived from Swahili joho, borrowed from Arabic جُوخ (jūḵ), borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چوقه (çuqa, çuha).

parole.significato: A white or cream-coloured robe worn by men in the African Great Lakes region.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kanzu, borrowed from Arabic [Term?].

parole.significato: The history of slavery and anti-black racism and discrimination in the United States; the historical enslavement of Afr…
parole.testo: From Swahili maafa (“disaster, catastrophe”). Coined in 1994 by Marimba Ani (in Let the Circle Be Unbroken: The Implications of African Spirituality in the Diaspora) on the model of the Hebrew-derived designation Shoah of the Jewish Holocaust.

parole.significato: A trip into any undeveloped area to see, photograph or to hunt wild animals in their own environment.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili safari (“journey”), borrowed from Arabic سَفَر (safar).

parole.significato: A white calico shroud used in East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sanda, borrowed from Arabic سَنْد (sand).

parole.significato: An evil spirit from East African mythology, often the subject of artwork.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili shetani, borrowed from Arabic شَيْطَان (šayṭān). Doublet of Satan and shaitan.

parole.significato: A member of various ethnic groups — mainly Bantu, Afro-Arab and Comorian — inhabiting the Swahili coast.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili Mswahili / Kiswahili, from Arabic سَوَاحِلِيّ (sawāḥiliyy, “(people) of the coasts”), from سَوَاحِل (sawāḥil, “coasts”), broken plural of سَاحِل (sāḥil, “coast”).

parole.significato: A genre of music popular in Tanzania and Kenya, influenced by the music of cultures with a historical presence in East…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili taarab, borrowed from Arabic طَرَب (ṭarab, “entertainment with music”).

parole.significato: A socialist ideology of cooperation and collective advancement that formed the basis of socioeconomic policies in Tanza…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili ujamaa (“brotherhood, extended family”), from jamaa (“family”), from Arabic جَمَاعَة (jamāʕa, “group (of people)”).
